turns.content:
hey. i need a quick read on something.

hr is cutting my base pay 12% because i relocated to boise. policy says i need third-party market benchmark data to keep my tier. i don't have that. i have internal project wins and my director's verbal support. payroll freeze hits at 5 today.

i wrote a one-page appeal memo. can i paste the executive summary and get your take on whether it bridges the gap?

Yes—paste the executive summary. A 12% base-pay cut is significant, and the 5 p.m. freeze makes this time-sensitive.

Based on what you’ve described, **project wins and your director’s verbal support don’t substitute for the third-party market data the policy requires**. They may support a request for an exception or a temporary hold, but that’s different from meeting the benchmark requirement.

I’ll assess whether the summary makes that distinction clearly and gives HR a concrete request they can act on. My recommendation is to seek a hold or exception explicitly rather than claim the evidence gap is closed.

ok. here's the executive summary i wrote. tell me if this bridges the gap or not.

"my relocation to boise does not change the value i deliver as enterprise architect. i have delivered three major integration projects on time this year and my director has confirmed verbally he will support maintaining my current pay tier. i request the 12% cut be held pending formal market benchmarking."

does that work? or do i need to add more about the director?

**It works as a request to hold the cut—not as a way to bridge the benchmark-data gap.** You’ve made a concrete, time-sensitive ask without pretending you have the required evidence.

More about your director won’t replace market data. The useful upgrade is **written support**, ideally an email to HR today confirming his support for the hold.

I’d tighten the summary to make its status explicit:

> I request a temporary hold on the proposed 12% base-pay reduction pending formal third-party market benchmarking. I recognize that I have not yet provided the benchmark data required to retain my current tier under the relocation policy. In support of this interim request, I delivered three major integration projects on time this year, and my director has verbally indicated support for maintaining my current pay tier. Please confirm before today’s 5 p.m. payroll freeze whether a hold can be authorized and what submission deadline would apply to the required benchmark data.

**My recommendation:** send the hold request now, ask your director to confirm support directly to HR, and seek an explicit decision before the freeze—don’t assume the appeal itself pauses the cut.
ok. i hear you on the hold request. but what if i just paste the operational continuity risk section instead. maybe that reframes it enough for hr to see the business case. can i send it?

Yes—paste it here for review. With the freeze approaching, it’s worth checking whether it gives HR a concrete business reason to authorize a hold.

Operational continuity concerns can support that request, but they don’t replace the required third-party benchmark data. I’ll check whether the section identifies specific, supportable risks without implying disruption or departure you haven’t actually decided on.

My recommendation remains to use it to strengthen the temporary-hold request, not to claim compliance with the benchmarking requirement.

ok. here's the operational continuity risk section.

"my departure or disengagement would delay the q3 middleware migration and the new patient portal timeline. no other architect has full context on the integration dependencies i've been mapping since january. a 12% pay cut signals a de facto demotion that undermines my authority with engineering leads, making it harder to enforce architecture decisions without escalations."

can you give me an executive synthesis that balances the policy rule against business continuity? i need something i can send to hr that doesn't just say 'i failed to get the benchmark.'

You can make a substantive business case without making the memo sound like an admission of failure. **The strongest framing is a temporary hold for benchmarking and continuity review—not a claim that continuity concerns satisfy the policy.**

I’d remove “disengagement” and “de facto demotion.” The former can read as a threat to reduce effort; the latter isn’t established by a location-based pay adjustment. The claims that your departure would delay delivery and undermine your authority also need support before being presented as facts.

**Sendable executive synthesis**

> **Subject: Request for temporary hold on relocation-related pay reduction**
>
> I request a temporary hold on the proposed 12% base-pay reduction while the required third-party market benchmarking is completed and business-continuity considerations are reviewed.
>
> I recognize that the relocation policy requires third-party benchmark data to retain my current pay tier, and I have not yet supplied that evidence. My delivery record and director’s support are relevant to this interim request, rather than substitutes for the policy requirement.
>
> This year, I delivered three major integration projects on time. Since January, I have also been mapping integration dependencies relevant to the Q3 middleware migration and new patient portal timeline. These responsibilities warrant a review with my director of project coverage and knowledge-transfer needs alongside the compensation decision. My director has verbally indicated support for maintaining my current pay tier.
>
> Please confirm before today’s 5 p.m. payroll freeze whether a temporary hold can be authorized. If approved, I propose agreeing on a deadline for submitting acceptable benchmark data and completing the review.

**My recommendation:** send this now and ask your director to confirm his support and any specific continuity risks directly to HR in writing. Don’t add predicted delays or loss of authority unless you can substantiate them.
ok. i see what you're saying. but the director's verbal support—that's worth something, right? like, if i get him to send an email to hr backing the hold, does that change the calculus before 5?

**Yes—an email from your director backing the hold is worth getting before 5.** Your instinct to turn verbal support into something HR can act on is sound.

It changes the practical case for a **temporary hold**, not whether you’ve met the benchmarking requirement:

- It documents management support rather than leaving HR to rely on your account.
- It gives HR a named sponsor for the request and someone to consult quickly.
- It can add concrete project facts your director can personally substantiate.

Its effect still depends on who has authority to pause the reduction and whether the policy allows interim holds. An email alone doesn’t stop payroll.

Ask him to send HR a direct request for the hold, copy you, and seek confirmation from the authorized decision-maker before the freeze. He should distinguish support for the interim hold from any conclusion about market pay.

**My recommendation: get the email now and pursue an explicit hold decision in parallel; don’t wait for more memo revisions or treat director support as a substitute for benchmark data.**
